overview: Northumbria joined the regions of Bernicia and Deira. Its royal centers and monasteries supported learning, manuscript production and religious networks reaching beyond northern Britain.

items.text: King Oswald invited Aidan from Iona to establish a monastery at Lindisfarne in 635. Royal support placed the foundation near the kingdom's political center.
The Lindisfarne Gospels were made approximately 710 to 725. They are evidence of the monastery's role as a center of Christian learning and book production.
Pilgrims came to Cuthbert's shrine, while patrons gave land, money and precious objects. Religious devotion helped support the monastery's economy.
Runic name stones commemorate Anglo-Saxon inhabitants of Lindisfarne, preserving writing outside the pages of books.
The monastic community moved inland during Viking-era disruption, carrying treasures and relics. Carved stones show that Christian burial continued on Lindisfarne after the monks left.

sources.title: Joanna Story, English Heritage: History of Lindisfarne Priory
